A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural-operator framework for compressed sensing MRI despite the changed title and author list. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fastMRI knee reconstruction experiments across undersampling patterns and rates, zero-shot super-resolution examples, and a cascade-scaling study.

after.justification: v2 reports original knee and brain reconstruction results, extended-field-of-view experiments, inference timings, and kernel-interpolation and parameter-matching controls.

M1.justification: The dual-domain unrolled reconstruction procedure, UDNO/DISCO building blocks, sensitivity-map estimation, and SSIM objective remain. NO-VN, KNO, and INO are renamed NO, NOk, and NOi. The extended-field-of-view experiment applies the existing resolution-agnostic architecture; the newly displayed loss equation restates the objective already documented in v1 Appendix B.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates fastMRI knee data. v2 additionally trains and evaluates on the fastMRI T2 brain subset and introduces zero-shot reconstruction beyond the training field of view using denser k-space inputs. These expand both anatomical coverage and the reconstruction scenarios actually tested.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained E2E-VN family, v2 evaluates zero-filled reconstruction, l1-Wavelet, U-Net, CSGM, ScoreMRI, PnP-DM, and an interpolated-kernel E2E-VN control. Diffusion reconstruction scores are reported for knee, not brain. v2 also separates equispaced-trained E2E-VN from fine-tuned E2E-VN++; v1 already fine-tuned its E2E-VN comparator, so the latter is not simply a wholly new method.

E3.justification: The principal experiments change from 20-epoch pretraining on 2x equispaced samples to 50 epochs on 4x samples, followed by 20-epoch fine-tuning. Pattern fine-tuning expands from three irregular patterns to all six patterns, and the main rate evaluation changes from 2/4/6/8x to 4/6/8/16x. New protocols include 160-to-320 k-space FOV testing and a 21.7M-parameter control trained for 10+1 epochs. The appendix also revises the reported k-space kernel cutoff from 0.04 to 0.02.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix D's study of 1, 4, and 8 cascades is removed. v2 instead tests whether CNN kernel resizing explains resolution robustness and whether performance differences persist with matched parameter counts. It also adds extended-FOV robustness examples and analysis of inference and pattern-specific tuning costs. These investigate substantially different explanatory and practical questions.

E5.justification: v1 presents point estimates and unbanded plots. v2 adds ± quantities in Tables 1, 2, and 5–7 and shaded bands in Figures 6 and 11. This adds variability reporting, but the quantities are not clearly defined and neither version specifies seeds, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 retains the original 2x PSNR comparison in Figure 1 but replaces the principal pattern/rate results under revised training conditions and adds brain, FOV, control, and timing results. New Table 1 reports knee PSNR of 39.14 versus 38.33 dB for NO and E2E-VN; Table 3 reports 0.06-second NO inference versus 84.46–96.16 seconds for diffusion methods. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1. The cascade-scaling results are removed.

T1.justification: The forward model, unrolled update, continuous convolution, DISCO quadrature approximation, and kernel basis expansion retain their mathematical substance. v2 separately numbers the initialization and explicitly writes the existing SSIM loss. Expanded resolution and kernel explanations introduce no substantive new derivation, theorem, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The unified reconstruction claim remains, but v2 adds extended-FOV reconstruction and a roughly 1,400x inference-speed advantage over diffusion as prominent claims. Its abstract replaces v1's maximum 4x NMSE reduction and 5 dB PSNR gain with average 11% SSIM and 4 dB PSNR improvements. The novelty claim changes from the first neural-operator application to MRI to the first resolution-agnostic MRI reconstruction framework.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning reliance on DISCO and the absence of diagnostic-accuracy evaluation, replacing v1's explicit fastMRI-resolution limitation. It also discusses residual artifacts after CNN kernel interpolation and explains efficiency differences through pattern-specific tuning requirements. These qualify and extend the retained resolution-agnostic interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access statement, coil and brain-subset details, RSS targets for diffusion comparisons, and explicit disclosure that super-resolution inputs and reference images use bilinear interpolation. Most UDNO specifications, learning rate, batch size, and hardware information remain. The k-space cutoff statement changes to 0.02, although its sentence is malformed; the earlier general single-cascade specification is no longer supplied for the expanded experiments.

R1.justification: The accelerated-MRI and neural-operator framing remains. Targeted additions include CSGM, PnP-DM, physics-informed neural operators, convolutional neural operators, and an SSIM reference; several background and k-space CNN references disappear. v2 emphasizes diffusion tuning costs and revises the novelty statement to a first resolution-agnostic MRI framework. Reference deduplication and publication updates do not constitute additional substantive changes.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction undergo substantial rewriting, the contribution list is reorganized, and the method narrative gains expanded DISCO explanations and a separate super-resolution subsection. Pattern and rate experiments become separate subsections, and Appendix D is restructured around different analyses. Terminology changes throughout from subsampling and NO-VN/KNO/INO to undersampling and NO/NOk/NOi.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensively revised figure sizing, captions, colors, and table organization. v2 adds a super-resolution schematic, expanded reconstruction panels, timing and brain tables, and control figures. The UDNO and mask illustrations are retained as Figures 7 and 8, while the cascade figure/table disappear; the original Figure 1 comparison is redisplayed rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's knee-only, single-comparator evidence through brain evaluation and controls addressing parameter count and CNN kernel resizing—important alternative explanations for the central architectural claim. Disclosure of interpolated super-resolution targets and the lack of diagnostic validation also makes the evidence easier to assess. These gains outweigh the lost cascade study and reporting weaknesses. Those weaknesses remain material: uncertainty quantities are undefined, and Section 4.2 attributes a 4.7 dB brain gain to irregular patterns although Table 6 implies about 10.18 dB; 4.7 dB instead matches the average across all patterns.
